title: Compact generation of the native derived module category
statement: Let S be an arbitrary ring in universe w. Choose a derived category of left S-modules in module universe max(w,vH) with Hom universe max(w,vH), and assume it has coproducts indexed by that universe. Then this derived category is compactly generated [def-pc-compactly-generated]: it admits a set-indexed compact family whose coproduct is a weak triangulated generator. The ring need not be commutative or nonzero.

source.place: First paragraph of the proof: D(Mod_R) is generated by the compact object R. Tag 07D9 supplies derived direct sums; for left modules use the opposite ring if the convention in the source is right modules.

proof.text: Place the free rank-one module ULift S in degree zero. Since it is projective its single complex is K-projective; maps from it into the nth shift identify naturally and additively with the nth cohomology module of the target.
Exact termwise direct sums commute with cohomology. The natural rank-one Hom calculation identifies the canonical direct sum of Hom groups with Hom into the derived coproduct, proving compactness.

If all maps from the rank-one object into shifts of K are zero, every cohomology module is zero, so K is acyclic and zero in the localization. Hence the rank-one object is a weak generator. Use a singleton compact family; its coproduct is canonically isomorphic to that object.

    {S : Type w} [Ring S]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{max w vH} (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S)]
    [HasCoproducts.{max w vH} (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S))] :

      (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S))
